lal.summary: For maybe first time since clinching Title No. 3,  they are building some momentum. Fab Four is clicking; Devean and D-Fish are helping.
Six guys scored all the points vs. Spurs. Fab Four scored 103 of the 120 points. Over long haul, Lakers will have to spread it more.
Lakes have best record, yeah, but have yet to look as good as they did Opening Night. L.A. stays up here because no one else is really rolling yet.
Kobe hasn't had to worry too much yet about negative fan reaction ... but Bulls haven't had to worry much yet about Lakers breaking their record. L.A.'s on a 64-18 pace, well shy of 72-10.
As loud as you can make a statement in November, Lakers just blared one with handy wins over Spurs and Pacers. They're starting to roll, people.
If Shaq keeps playing D this way, we'll be down to two threats to L.A.'s title aspirations. Injury and boredom.
No one's hurt, so it must have been boredom. Or maybe Mavs (then Blazers) simply outplayed the consensus No. 1 squad. At both ends.
It probably isn't much consolation, but losing to Dallas seems to have tripped up the hated Mavs' season as much as it helped them, judging by Dallas' week.
Three future Hall of Famers, apparently, ain't enough. Perhaps the shame of a slip in these here rankings will spark the Mailman-less Lakers back to life.

Attn. Geniuses: There's no point bombarding the committee with e-mails about all those early wins over the Spurs when the Lakers are looking at two disturbing injuries and keep losing to teams SA would pummel now.
If you don't believe us, listen to Rick Fox, who told our ESPN.com colleague Peter May: 'I think we have a bigger mountain to climb than we're willing to admit.'
The on-court performance has actually picked up; kudos to Kareem (Rush) and Slava. But the gloomy forecasts for Shaq, Kobe and Mailman easily could have warranted a steeper drop.
Recent results haven't been great, and Mailman's prognosis is getting worse by the day, but it's a fine week when Kobe returns and Shaq announces he'll also be back soon.
With a month's worth of road games to come, Mailman out 'til mid-March and Kobe freshly injured ... Phil Jackson will surely see this as a good time for Shaq to get angry and start moving people.
Don't believe us if you don't want to. Payton says so, too: Lakers' Big Four have to get some court time together BEFORE the playoffs start to re-establish some rhythm.
It appears those Shaq and Phil contract extensions have been put on hold until Lakers determine whether they can hold onto Kobe. Doesn't it?
Even on a 6-1 run, can't say they have momentum yet. Not in the midst of a stretch where 11 of 15 are on the road.
Cynic in me says they're actually trying to create controversy to create a spark. Because they need a spark: Lakers are 4-11 against winning teams since Dec. 4.
Says Kobe, apparently going for Understatement O' The Season: "It's an odd year." Truth is, there hasn't been a moment's peace since the day after Malone and Payton held their joint press conference.

Now that the Lakers have survived the toughest part of the schedule and close with 13 of their final 16 games at Staples, we ask: Why on Earth are they letting Kobe play when he admits his shoulder ain't right?
Winning? Yes. Impressing? Not yet. Not when they're struggling to put away bad teams or even keep them out of the hundreds.
OK, maybe it's not solely Kobe. Lakers are 8-1 with Mailman back in the lineup ... and thus back to No. 1 for the first time in 14 weeks.

One loss, however disconcerting, can't drop them too far. Let's face it: Lakers are still a servicable 27-7 when all four of the future Hall of Famers play. That's a 65-win pace over 82 games, for what it's worth.

If we overreacted like many did when Lakers routed Kings, we'd be saying Lakers are finished now. But you rely on us as a voice of a reason, so: It's the next drama, in the playoffs, that would be truly worrisome. Not Sunday's inexplicable no-show.

sas.summary: Without Parker, and with Rasho starting (very) slowly, yet another clunky Spurs start is little surprise.
System is so effective, Spurs can lose Duncan and plug Jason Hart (who?) in for Parker and still play Lakers and Mavs evenly. Opponents better enjoy Spurs' injury plight while it lasts.
Full squad is together for first time since Paris exhibition trip. Now to see how long it takes for some rhythm.
Of all the guys Spurs lost -- Admiral Robinson, Stephen Jackson, Danny Ferry -- who knew they'd miss Steve Kerr (the shooter) most? SA better pick it up from the perimeter if it wants to repeat.
Sorry. Even without Admiral Dave -- and even accounting for the ankle injuries suffered by Duncan and Parker -- Spurs shouldn't be 2-6 on the road. Just like we said about Mavs.
Pop was forced to trot out the line about 'more room for improvement than anyone else' awfully early. Committee might look silly if Pop's not right.
Didn't see this one coming, either, but Spurs suddenly have the longest active win streak in the whole league. Last place no more.
Rasho's D can't be that bad, because Spurs have held the opposition under 80 points 13 times already ... and they're 13-0 in those games.
Thirteen straight wins. Allowing 76.4 ppg over last 12 games. Does it really matter that the opposition hasn't been the toughest?
Not going to drop SA after one ugly loss because the 13-0 run was so good. But Tim Duncan's free-throw woes are bordering on unforgivable. You've been warned, Spurs.

Yet again we say: Rasho can't be that bad defensively if Spurs are on pace to set a single-season record for PPG allowed. Hawks gave up 83.4 in lockout-shorted 1999 season; SA at 82.5 with Rasho in place of Admiral Dave.
A four-spot drop is the Power Rankings equivalent of a loud Popovich scolding. Spurs deserve it, too, after defense that can't lose (16-0) when opponents are held below 80 disappaears for a week.
Remember when you could just blame everything on the free-throwing? At 3-5 since a 16-1 run, it's obviously more than FTs.

Draw a line under the top seven, because the NBA's elite is only seven deep. The confusing part: How on Earth have free-throw woes snowballed into a broader malaise that has dropped the defending champs all the way to No. 7?
If it's February, Spurs are on the road and rolling anew. Now to see if the SBC Center rodeo really kick-starts the defending champs' season, like it did last season.

My friends in Minny don't like seeing Spurs up here, but it's February and the defending champs are rolling again on cue. Of course, if Spurs want to stay up here, they have to keep rolling this time ... and make their bloody free throws.

They're just about the hottest team out West. They're pretty much the healthiest. So they're tops after completing their annual February trek at 6-1, bouncing back from that Cleveland loss to win the game (in Minny) that mattered most.
Upset O' The Week: Committee received only a few e-mails suggesting that our Spurs-to-conference finals pick caused the jinx that felled Duncan.
Who knew Duncan was holding them back? Rasho averages 17.0 ppg, 12.4 rpg and 3.4 bpg during a 4-1 run without TD ... during which Spurs top 100 points three times.
They can actually win points with us by taking an uber-cautious approach with Duncan. He shouldn't have played at all last week, if you ask us, because no playoff seed is worth rushing back for.
The reason they're so skittish about Duncan's injury: Spurs don't have anyone else on the roster with a career scoring average higher than Parker's 13.1 ppg.
As Detroit discovered, Spurs are pretty unbeatable when they hold the opposition under 80. 22-0 now, in fact.

They always get it going during the last 40 games of the season and it's happening again. A 5-0 finish would make the Spurs' finishing kick a tidy 30-10 this time. Over the past five years, Spurs' average finish is -- you guessed it -- 30-10.

Running out of time to snatch the divison title from Minnesota, Spurs can still point to a nine-game win streak -- with an average victory margin of 13.7 points -- that suggests they're looking better than decent as the playoffs approach.

sac.summary: Good spot for Kings, given that they followed Spurs into Denver short-handed and, just like short-handed Spurs, took little Nuggets lightly.
Who knew, without Webber, that defense would suffer most? Kings giving up points like they did in J-Will era.
Relax, people. Maloofs won't be moving Kings away from league's most rabid fan base to relocate to North Coast Plaza in Anaheim. Worry more about Kings' D and the recent double-digit blown leads.
A win at plucky Utah, followed by eight straight home games, should alleviate some of the recent panic in Sacto while Webber rehabs. Kings slipped a spot only because Hornets' week was so fab.
Since blowing that big lead in Portland, Kings are 7-0 with 18-point average margin of victory. Without Webber. Impressive even with a cushy, home-heavy schedule.
With a win over Minny on Friday, Kings are a certain No. 2. OT loss to Wolves made us hesitate a bit.
Clearly still Kings of playing hurt, surpassing 15-5 start without Webb in 2001-02. But the road beckons.
It's a good thing they're playing so well without Webber. Because he's going to end up missing more time than anyone expected, Webb included.
Christmas Day blown lead vs. Dallas was a downer, as was the news that Chris Webber can't even scrimmage yet ... but Kings are still on their own little 17-4 run.
Only real strike against Kings so far: They've only played one of 12 games vs. Spurs, Mavs and Lakers ... and lost it.
Great news (for us): Sacramento can get mad at someone else this week. Larry Bird, from afar, says Peja needs to broaden his offensive repertoire.

Sacto's automatic promotion was denied when injuries took all the meaning out of Friday's Laker rout. More damning than the fact it seems like Kings play every game at home is the slip from No. 1 in the league to No. 23 in defensive field-goal percentage.

Can't say schedule is easy anymore, in midst of a stretch with 12 of 17 games on the road. A 2-3 start to that stretch also means (again) that you can't spew ridiculous stuff about Kings not needing Webber.
Given that Kings so easily could have gone 0-3 to start six-game trip, the 3-0 flourish Sacto finished with was maybe the most impressive thing seen yet in its Webber-less season.
Nationally televised loss to Spurs was disheartening, but Kings' hold on the top spot is preserved by the fact that it was only San Antonio's first big win of the season.
Six, eight, 10 more games without Webber? No prob, even with 19 of the last 32 games on the road. Of course, this assumes Webb doesn't miss a minute of May or June.
Check that: If Webber's still out and Miller and Jackson join him, that could be a problem. Of course, the Kings being the Kings, it hasn't been a huge problem yet.
The whole team is smokin' hot right now: Peja, Bibby, Vlade. And Miller's back. And Webb returns Tuesday. Committee's feeling even better about that Kings-to-conference finals pick.
Don't forget that they're STILL not at full strength. Only when Bobby Jax comes back will Kings really have a bench.
Sacto's not terribly concerned about Webber matching Iverson's 2-for-21 effort. Going 1-3 against Portland, a potential first-round foe, is more of a red flag.
Webber's back, but Kings are still looking for last season's defense. There's no sign of it yet, with Sacto sitting in the league's bottom seven in PPG allowed and defensive FG pct.

We're not going to lump in every Kings fan, but whoever's booing Webber is so far out of the line that the line is a dot to the boobirds. This guy put Sacramento on the NBA map, kept Kings there by staying there, and he doesn't get a grace period?

If Webber can't get his body to at least 80 percent, and if Miller and Bobby Jax don't heal in time for the playoffs, you can expect to hear more of that Window Is Closing stuff. Kings just can't get back to the conference finals if not at full strength.
For weeks they've looked lifeless, like Kings were waiting for something to spark them into attack mode. Not surprisingly, it was a Lakers visit that woke 'em up.

dal.summary: 'Toine's doing OK for a guy who has practiced four times. Ditto for Delk. And now that they've all recovered from the gray uniform fiasco ...
You know there's a scoring problem out there when Mavs go for 71 and 81 points in back-to-back games. And they had Nash back in uniform for the second one.
Jamison admits that this whole Sixth Man thing is major adjustment ... so perhaps 'Tawn ain't the favorite to win that award.
Never thought we'd say this but: If Mavs start making their threes, they might really be high-scoring. Amazingly, Mavs are 20th in league from deep.

Unsavory as it is to even suggest, Fortson foul was a rare bit of nasty from Mavs, something critics always say they need. More critical: Mavs need to start playing like the road juggernaut they've been in recent seasons; 2-6 is shocking from them.
Bright spot in Nowitzki's absence: Josh Howard is playing like All-Rookie Team material. That said, Mavs would prefer not to face Lakers sans Dirk again Friday.
We'd like to claim we saw that win over the Lakers coming -- after a fall-from-ahead loss to Clips in same building -- but at least we were ahead of the curve on Josh Howard.

Relying on your offense is fine, but the plan doesn't work when your FG and FT shooting slip noticeably and the road -- 3-9 after a league-leading mark of 27-14 last season -- starts to look as tough as it did during the extremely dark 1990s.

Mavs are 5-8 when Finley or Nowitzki is missing, but they're supposed to be deep enough to overcome one such injury. Weird thing is they're also supposed to have trouble against the league's elite, but Mavs are 5-3 against the top four.

Always good for a paradox, Mavs are 6-3 vs. Spurs, Kings, Lakers and Wolves, after going 6-10 against same four last season. Dallas, meanwhile, is 4-4 vs. Rockets, Nuggets, Grizz, Clips and Warriors, after going 20-0 against same five last season.

Doesn't look like a single Mav will earn an All-Star spot in Los Angeles. Doesn't look like a single Mav could argue with that sentiment, which is why another trade grows more inevitable by the minute.
Even accounting for failure to land 'Sheed and latest Nellie-Cubes saga, it was a fine week. Even defensively ... in flashes.
Make that 8-3 vs. Wolves, Kings, Lakers and Spurs. Mavs suddenly look like a team trying to convince their bosses that they don't need another trade.

If anybody was unjustly omitted from the Stein Line List O' Reserves, it's Michael Finley. He has been turning back the clock lately, so put Fin on the list with Bibby, Nash and Payton for one West reserve guard spot.
A brief visit from German shot doctor Holger Geschwindner, as always, has snapped Nowitzki's shooting stroke back on kill. Dirk's shot had previously flattened out a bit.
Gutty little Mavs definitely got hot as the break approached, finishing on a 13-3 kick. Good thing, too, because it looks like this is their team.
Returned from the All-Star break with a thud at Memphis ... and there's worse news if the standings hold and serve up a first-round matchup with L.A.

Very quietly, Mavs are smokin' hot themselves: 18-4 in their last 22 and 9-3 vs. Kings, Wolves, Spurs and Lakers. Their March schedule is brutal, though, which should make it tough to continue this second-half surge.
So much for momentum. Mavs better get a top-four seed if they want to reach the second round, because they've lost all confidence in their formerly unquestioned ability to win on the road.
Having finally found a couple of teams they can beat on the road -- Suns and Clips -- you get the feeling the Mavs' next quest is finding a way to avoid the Lakers in Round 1.
The success of their trades remains debatable. But they sure had a great draft, getting Josh Howard at No. 29 and signing Marquis Daniels as an FA when Daniels went undrafted.
With Mavs' defense, you expect problems. But chemistry has never been a Mavs problem in this era. Until now, it seems.
Everyone knows about the switch back to Small Ball. The better news, quite possibly, is Mavs' standing as the healthiest team in the West's top six. It's something.

On the season's list of unexplained occurences, the disappearance of Dallas' killer instinct on the road is way up there. After going 27-14 in road games each of the past two seasons, now they can't even win at Golden State, falling to 15-25.

min.summary: 61-pointer in Jersey was ugly, but if you're keeping score: Wally and Troy are still out; Spree and Kandi are playing hurt.
Florida road trip was timely tonic for team still missing Wally and Troy. Playing shorthanded might be wearing on KG, who's on pace to ring up 47 Ts.

Two bad home losses (Seattle and Utah) send Wolves tumbling into Midwest cellar. They're only 1 1/2 games out of first, true, but it's been a disappointing start, even when you factor in Wally and Troy injuries.
Playing better? Yes. Beating better teams? Not yet. Wolves don't have one win over a team you'd call a playoff lock, but they rise by default.
As with Spurs, injuries have undoubtedly been a factor. Like Spurs, Wolves still should be better than 9-8 with whoever's healthy. They won't be up here much longer if it continues.
Still don't have anything close to their full team, but Wolves just gave us our first glimpse of the team we expected to see. And the Spree we expected to see.
On top of all the injuries, Wolves have blown four leads after starting the fourth quarter ahead. It happened only three times all last season.
Not fully healthy yet (Wally) and not winning at home yet (7-5), but Wolves are starting to show us glimpses of the good squad they're supposed to be.
And your new leader in the Plus/Minus Standings: Wolves at +7, seven more road wins than home defeats.
Pacers just passed 'em in the Plus/Minus Standings -- Indy has eight more road wins than home defeats, compared to Minny's seven -- and so Pacers pass 'em here, too.
At 19-6 since their 5-5 start, it's safe to say Wolves have started to click. Safe to say, too, that they've nudged Dallas out of the West's top four for now.
Top spot had Wolves' name all over it after the back-to-back wins at Hornets and Spurs. Couldn't do it, though, after that Houston performance.
At this rate, Sam I Am is going to L.A. for sure with KG and they just might be bringing Flip with them. Now 24-7 since starting 5-5.
Sorry. Wolves have just been too complacent since promotion to No. 1 for my, Flip's and KG's liking. Maybe a drop to No. 2 can snap them back into focus.
With no clear-cut powerhouse established and lots of competition up here, a couple losses these days can send you tumbling. Wolves just found that out.
Still no lasting glimpse of Wally World, but Kandi is on his way back. The Wolves will need their depth now so Sam and Spree save something for the playoffs.
Had they beaten the Spurs, the top spot was theirs. No. 2 ain't bad, though, for the West's first team to reach 40 wins.
Let's see how Wolves respond to the worst loss of the season. But let's not forget, even after losing to Iverson-less Philly, that Wolves are a tidy 38-12 since their 5-5 start.
One bad loss to the Iverson-less Sixers was forgivable. But this?  Committee could have dropped Wolves lower after two more curious home losses, the second coming to ... Boston?

Maybe it's just one of those freaky coincidences. Or maybe Wolves, now 0-5 in their past five Sunday games, better concentrate on fixing this problem before they get to the playoffs, when there are lots of games on Sundays.

Responding to the embarrassing factoids about them in this space last week, Wolves have finally won a Sunday game after losing five Sundays in a row. Now to see if they can steady themselves and hold off Spurs for the West's No. 2 seed.
Team record for wins is 51. Of course, before this 7-8 slump, Wolves were on pace to win 60.
With all the hubbub surrounding Lakers and now Spurs, Wolves are quietly putting themselves back together as well. At the right time, too.
Evidence to prove these aren't Wolves of old? KG (the MVP) and Co. are 8-4 against Spurs, Lakers and Kings.

nop.summary: Don't even need to look it up to know that a Tim Floyd team has never been higher in the Power Rankings. Of course, Baron has something to do with it.
Yikes. Did we just put three East teams in top four? Baron's getting his way these days.
Perhaps in preparation for next season's move to West, Hornets are shooting more 3-pointers than anyone. A drop was unavoidable, though, after Dallas showed them how it's done in 28-point rout.
Coach Floyd, whose best season in Chicago netted 17 wins, is already more than halfway to No. 18. Of course, with the Bulls, he never had anyone like Baron.
Why do the Hornets always do this? As soon as they start looking good ... they lose to the Heat and Knicks and almost lose to Cavs.
Floyd got his win in Chicago, but Hornets are 4-3 since win at Detroit and lost at home to only likely playoff opponent (Houston) in that stretch.
Groovin' again, but discovered they might need Mash after all ... after Baron goes through 9-for-68 stretch on 3-pointers.
Floyd gets magic win No. 18, highest total of his career, but only after Hornets get waxed on the road twice (Clippers, Nuggets) and lose at home to Sacto.
Baron Davis started spectacularly but needs to play smarter, especially with Mash out longer than expected. In past 15 games, Baron is 30-for-140 on 3s. That's 21 percent.

Great line by ESPN.com contributor Peter May: Hornets need Mash back ASAP, or else Baron's right arm might fall off. Davis has made 101 3-pointers -- 25 more than No. 2 Peja Stojakovic -- but has needed 321 attempts to do so.
Mash's recovery is taking longer than expected and Mash-less Hornets are 5-8 since 17-7 start. Hence the slip out of the top 10.
No longer is anyone worrying about how Mash will handle re-meshing with a team that now plays at Baron's pace. Question now is: How soon can Mash get back and keep Hornets from slipping further?
Comeback in SA sans Baron was inspiring. News that Baron and Mash could be back this week is even more of a lift.
Very nearly went 0-3 in Mash's first week back. So, yeah: Hornets are still getting readjusted to each other.
More fodder to back the argument that the Hornets shouldn't be sending two to the All-Star Game: Since 17-7 start, they're 10-17.

Imagine that: After we said so about a zillion times, the Hornets are finding it's not so easy to mesh Davis' run-and-gun game with Mash's preference for post-ups. It's nothing personal between them, just a clash of styles.
Still struggling to capture November form, but let's face it: On talent, there's no way the Hornets should slip out of the East's top four.
Only 7-8 since Mash returned, and there are empty seats aplenty already in the Bayou. We'd like to say things will get better, but Hornets have only three months left in the Leastern Conference.
It's not Mash, who has already nailed two game-winning shots since coming back from injury. Floyd better figure out whatever it is, or else he won't have a winning record here, either.
Among Floyd's problems at present is Hornets' away form: Since getting to 13-13 on the road, NO has lost six straight on its travels.
Uh-oh: A loss to Pistons on Tuesday would be the third straight at home, with six of the next seven on the road thereafter. Hornets have dropped seven straight roadies.
Yikes. Baron- and Mash-less Hornets have dropped eight straight on the road ... and play seven of their final nine games on the road.
In immediate danger: Hornets' record of 11 straight seasons at .500 or better, and their streak of seven straight winning seasons. And Tim Floyd, of course.

As bumpy as the second half has been, Hornets don't want this season to end. Not with Floyd barely clinging to his job and not after Hornets went 11-17 against the conference that beckons next season.

bkn.summary: None of East's supposed elite has looked especially impressive so far. Truth is, though, K-Mart's ankle scare jolted Nets more than Opening Night loss at Toronto.
To protect Zo, with K-Mart already out, Lord Byron keeps bringing Mourning off bench. But there's a new concern: Is Kidd logging too many minutes?
Injuries have played a part, no question, but Nets' lackluster start has already raised the question: Are they giving Byron their best?

Can't say it better than the ailing J-Kidd: "Once we get to the embarrassment stage, we start playing." If that lack of sustained intensity continues, Nets won't even be in the teens much longer. They're 2-5 at home, compared to last season's 18-1 start.

Sad news of 'Zo's retirement means Kidd just lost one of the main reasons he stayed in Jersey. Staying in the easier East was another reason, but Nets, at best, rank fourth in East after a month ... and won't climb with effort they're giving.
With Kidd playing at estimated 75 percent, Nets can only start with small steps. Step 1: Beating Seattle on Tuesday would secure season's first three-game win streak.
The four-game win streak obviously wasn't a cure-all. The consolation: Memphis is off the schedule until the NBA Finals.
Ever so briefly, Nets were over .500 (13-12) for first time since they were 2-1. Not surprisingly, the good cheer felt around the club was also brief.
Things change fast around here: Nets, without warning, look more together than anyone in the East.
Dare we say Jason Kidd is back to something close to full health: He's averaging 22.8 points, 10.5 assists and 8.2 rebounds in six games since Christmas.
Nets are 9-3 since Kidd's tirade about the coaching. Which means he'll have to break his "no tirades" New Year's resolution if the Nets slump again.

Brooklyn Nets. Doesn't exactly roll off the tongue, does it? Of course, with seven of next eight games on the road -- starting at Dallas and San Antonio, back-to-back -- Nets have more pressing questions to answer.
Despite best efforts to keep sliding and forfeit this status, the Nets are one of only eight teams outside Midwest Division with a record above .500. Midwest has six such teams.

If any team is going to make it an Elite Eight, it's Lawrence Frank's Nets. But only if Frank's 3-0 start means Jersey's players realize that it's on them now, with their excuse (Lord Byron) dismissed to the golf course.
Jersey has indeed confirmed already that we do have an Elite Eight in this league. Under Frank, the Nets are playing how they should have been all season.
Ten straight wins is 10 straight wins, no matter the opposition. And if Lawrence Frank never loses, those Doogie Howser jokes might actually stop.
Said so when Spurs and Pistons went on their long streaks and have to say so again: 13 wins in a row is 13 wins in a row, no matter who the opposition is. Could Nets still be the East's beast?
A 14-2 record in the Lawrence Frank era is still sparkling, but Nets' status as East favorite will continue to be questioned if they don't start beating some quality opposition.

With the Atlantic locked up, and with only a mathematical hope of catching Indiana, Nets would be wise to let J-Kidd keep sitting and recharging. They can beat Pistons in Round 2 without home-court advantage, but only if Kidd is at full capacity.

It's tough to celebrate Kidd's 59th triple-double, good for a tie with Larry Bird for fourth all-time, in the same week K-Mart tweaks an ankle. It's only a tweak, apparently, but that's scary enough for a team that's not deep.

Can't say the honeymoon's over, because it's not fair to judge Nets when J-Kidd and K-Mart are out injured. But it's safe to say Nets are sweating, banged up and now 6-8 since that 13-0 start under Lawrence Frank.
What would concern me now, if I were a Nets fan like our good friend and research ace Sanford Appell: Wearing out Jefferson while J-Kidd and K-Mart are recuperating.

Tough to watch without Kidd and K-Mart, but facts is facts: Nets have three straight Atlantic titles. Before this, Nets hadn't seen three straight winning SEASONS in the NBA since a stretch of four straight from 1981-82 thorugh '84-85.

Wins in their last two games, at Atlanta and at Miami, would give Nets their first winning road record in their NBA history. Not that it really matters if J-Kidd and K-Mart can't make it through the playoffs.

ind.summary: Huge boost for Carlisle when Pacers outdueled Pistons in Detroit ... followed by major letdown for Carlisle when Pacers lost home opener to Bucks.
Whatever Carlisle is doing with Artest, he should keep doing it, because Artest is looking -- gasp -- composed. Playing well, too.
West clearly didn't take kindly to last week's Power Rankings kindness shown to East. Only Indy had a decent response to its promotion.
Fearless prediction: If Indy doesn't lose a road game all season, it'll win the East and have home-court advantage in the Finals.
Can't come down on them too hard for losing in L.A. Rest of West Coast trip (Phoenix, Portland, Seattle and Sacramento) will determine how tough WE are on them.
OK. Now let's see how Pacers respond, after 2-3 trip that should have been no worse than 3-2 ... and after Artest's first slip.
Just a so-so week, but Pacers remain the only team around that can say it hasn't lost more than one in a row.
7-0 record after a loss is admirable -- no one in the league can match it -- but 6-6 record since 14-2 start is more than a little disconcerting.
Big week for Isiah Thomas, who gets a new job in New York ... then gets to watch his old team plunge into turmoil even sooner than last season.
After the recent chaos, you can make the argument -- and we do -- that this 4-0 response is better than the 14-2 start.
7-1 since Artest and Carlisle clashed, and the back-to-back in Texas -- beating Dallas and nearly beating San Antonio -- was a big credibility boost for the East's best team.

Viva Las Least: We've seen enough from Pacers, halfway in, to guarantee that there will not be another 11-19 finish this season. This promotion is their reward for making the oft-bashed East a bit legit.
Can't help but admit that it's somewhat humbling to see that the Power Rankings jinx can still hang with the Men's Fitness jinx. As Pacers can now testify.
If we were Pacer People, we'd be a lot more panicky about O'Neal's neck and Artest's thumb as opposed to sweating the bloody rankings.
In spite of that loss in the Isiah Bowl, Indy is on a 17-4 surge. Of course, the Pacers need to be that hot to stay in the top three with all the West timber.
J. O'Neal said Sunday that Pacers believe they can beat any West foe in a seven-game series. Pacers have to start by winning a few seven-gamers in the East.

Tough to be optimistic today if Artest is out for the rest of the regular season. Yet Indy's lead in the East is such that there is one positive: Artest's fill-ins have a cushion to make a few mistakes.
Indy's bucking to be Kings O' The East. As in Kings O' The Playing Hurt. Despite losing Artest, Pacers have won seven of nine.
It was 23 games ago that the committee said there would be no second-half fade from Pacers. Turns out they're getting stronger, starting with Artest's speedy recovery.
Hate to tease our good friends in Indy ... but your Pacers were a win in Cleveland away from securing the top spot for the first time in eight weeks and just the second time all season.

In the midst of a rare losing streak -- its first since Jan. 24 -- it should be pointed out that Carlisle is about to become only the second coach in league history (along with Pat Riley) to win division titles in each of his first three full seasons.
We'll say the same thing about Jermaine that we said about Kobe initially: Why not let JO sit a little longer? Especially with all the winning Indy has been doing without him.

Consolation prizes after Detroit stifled Pacers to make it a rare two-loss week: Indy needs just a 3-2 finish to be the winningest Pacer team in the club's NBA history, and a 4-1 finish to be the league's only 60-win team.

Uncle Reg says pendulum has swung in Pistons' favor and away from the only team out there that can win 60 games. We're a little surprised he'd say so, but we'll let the playoffs settle whether or not it's some psychological ploy.

det.summary: First Larry loses to coach he replaced, then he's implicated in an Iverson rip job. Not the best week for Coach Brown.
Haven't lost since Opening Night. Better yet, have never seen Big Ben score the way he's scoring, up to 11 ppg from 7.
It isn't much, but it's something: Consolation for Pistons is knowing that some rough West road losses are already out of the way.
Beating Lakers at home was reassuring ... but Pistons are now an alarming 0-4 in games decided by five points or less. Can't believe previously clutch Chauncey missed those two FTs vs. NO.
With Chauncey getting all the pub, Rip heats up and goes for 44, then 25. Easiest thing to say is they make a good backcourt tandem.
With five more road wins than home defeats, Pistons trail only Indy (+7) and L.A. (+6) in that category.
No, Larry's not going to leave. Way too early for that. But that's all we can say definitively, with Pistons gripped by a sudden teamwide bout of indecisiveness.
The riddle no one in Detroit can explain: Pistons went 14-6 in first 20 ... and NOW they're confused and tentative because of Larry's system?
Finding it tough to score, much less win. Seven times in last 12 games, Pistons haven't even scored 80.
They needed this five-game win streak badly. Because the Pistons are still just 7-7 in their past 14 games, in spite of their record run of 36 straight games holding the opposition under 100 points.
Mavs couldn't beat these guys Sunday, but maybe they can learn from them. About two weeks ago, Pistons looked as bad as Dallas does today. Now look at Larry's squad.

Detroit deserves to be even higher, because 12 wins in a row -- like we said with San Antonio's recent 13-gamer -- is 12 wins in a row no matter who the opposition is. Problem is, how do you put Pistons any higher with the way top three are rolling?
Power Rankings jinx is still so potent that merely hinting Pistons were closing in on the top three resulted in an 0-3 stretch after a 13-game win streak.
Detroit's rolling back in the right direction after a few pedestrian wins, but Larry would be the first to tell you: Coaches are hired to ... quit and find a new gig.
The jokes about Larry's habit of moving around will always persist ... but it's safe to say that you can scratch Dallas off the list of potential destinations after Brown's back-and-forth with Cuban.

The way Pistons are playing, we're back to a Super Seven as opposed to an Elite Eight. They're still here simply because they're still an East title contender ... but only if they wake up immediately.

Detroit clings to its top-eight spot because Joe D pulls off Heist O' The Season by getting 'Sheed before the trade buzzer. But it's a different story on the floor: 0-2 with 'Sheed, 1-8 in the last nine games.
We kept Pistons in the top eight last week when they were in the midst of a 1-8 stretch. So they stay here now, even after a 4-0 week, until we can get a better read on how they look with 'Sheed.
Larry is never satisfied, but not even he can complain this week after Pistons became the first team in the shot-clock era to hold three straight opponents under 70. Can he?
As stingy as they've been lately, Pistons can't escape the fact that they're 1-5 vs. Indy and Jersey. The good news: 'Sheed didn't play in any of those six games.

If defense wins championships, or at least gets you to the Finals from the East, you can understand why Pistons are feeling so good about themselves. And since they've been more consistent than anyone else lately, East or West, here's a healthy bump.

We go out on a limb for Pistons and look what we get? Two losses, and two hobbled Wallaces. Blame the supposed Power Rankings jinx all you want, but no one will have that crutch in the playoffs, when there are no Power Rankings.
After absolutely swamping Indiana, Detroit is closer to the defensive record than San Antonio at 84.4 ppg allowed. If only they got  'Sheed sooner.

At 19-5 since adding 'Sheed, the only real concern is Detroit's 6-12 record in games decided by three points or less. Only four other playoff teams (Nuggets at 3-9, Nets at 3-7, Spurs at 6-8, Heat at 6-7) are under .500 in those circumstances.

phx.summary: First example of higher expectations: Suns lose to Spurs, then Lakers, and people start asking "What's wrong?"
Fans just voted Mark West as best center in franchise history. Helps explain why Suns hounded Wiz until they'd got Jahidi White.
Until Warriors lost Sunday night, Suns were only West team -- out of 14 -- with sub-.500 record. So, no, they're not handling burden of expectations very well so far.

Suns moved up so much on same principle ... who below them is clearly better right now? At least beating a few East stragglers (Chicago, Orlando, Miami) took some heat off Frank Johnson, who shares hot seat with Bulls' Cartwright.
They weren't ready for the big jump, apparently. After losing to Denver by 30, then beating Mavs by 31, only thing that's clear is that Frank Johnson is still under fire.
Suns clearly haven't quit on Frank Johnson, or themselves, but they have wasted a friendly early schedule.
Now that they've changed coaches, and they're still struggling, Suns will have to blame the Curse of the No. 8 Seed. Phoenix and Orlando are apparently both victims.
West was tough enough when they had Amare. Without him they're 2-7 -- 2-5 since D'Antoni took over.
It's officially a trend: Amare, like Webber and Mash and AI, is out the dreaded LONGER THAN EXPECTED. Guess someone in the West has to be way below .500.
That's (life without) Amare: Suns needed Golden State to lose five in a row just to get close to someone else in the West.
Fun while it lasted: Can't use our That's (life without) Amare comment intro anymore now that Stoudemire has been activated. We'll work on something Zarko-related now that he's back, too.
Can't see Suns going much higher, but the ball is moving more without Steph ... and they're no longer looking like West's biggest underachievers.
For a second there, it looked like new Suns were on the rise. Then came three painful losses (Nuggets, Spurs, Wolves) by total of 11 points.

It's tough to get too hyped up about Joe Johnson's hot streak when there are echoes in the desert about Amare not wanting to play through some pain. Not a storyline you expected to hear about the Suns' manchild.
Again, it's good to see Joe Johnson playing well ... but the Suns have lost nine of 11, which overshadows Johnson's 23.4 ppg over the last nine games and Amare's 10-block party.
Second-half goals are clear: Trade Googs and/or Jahidi and keep losing their way up the lottery ladder.
Traded Googs and became first West team to lose 40 games. The Suns are meeting their build-for-the-future objectives, in other words.
At least Amare has hushed his critics since winning MVP honors in the Rookie Game in L.A. Amare has averaged 26 ppg in Suns' past eight games and has been throwing down some sick dunks lately.
Phoenix has a chance to ruin someone else's season with three cracks at Mavs in the next 14 games. Beyond that, there's not a lot going on here.
If Colangelo ends up selling his majority interest before next season, he'll go out with Suns' worst season since 1987-88, when they went 28-54.

Touching as it was to hear The Chuckster say he wants to enter the HOF as a Sun, the starving fans in the desert will be dealt another blow when they find out that players don't go in with specific teams in basketball's HOF. That's a baseball thing.
Committee still likes Dice enough to say that a Dice-Amare-Marion front line sounds intriguing. Doesn't it?
Uh-oh. Suns need a 3-2 finish to avoid the club's worst record since a 28-54 mark in 1987-88. Four of those last five games are at home, but the comp is tough: Denver, Sacto, Memphis and Utah.
If there's a worthy MIP complaint out there, it's that we neglected to list Joe Johnson as a nominee. He's one of the few bright spots in a mostly dark season in the desert.

bos.summary: Big jump is a nod to Vin Man's early efforts (15.7 ppg, 6.0 rpg). Now degree of difficulty increases: Celts visit Pistons, then host Nets and Kings.
Don't like the white shoes at home, but still likin' Vin Man's comeback. He just put up his first double-double as a Celt, and leads league in FG pct.
Theory that Pierce would score 30 nightly might have missed. Shooting woes are one factor, but he's actually playing more of a team game with 'Toine gone.
On second thought, Pierce is playing more of a subdued game than a team game. He's in a shooting and scoring funk.
Pierce called them soft and two folds against Knicks make it tough to argue. Weird thing is, Celts are 2-0 against West teams (Grizz and Kings).
Not sure what's scarier for a coach: Obie's recent vote of confidence ... or huge blown lead at home vs. Suns. At least Celts bounced back to give their coach a nice win at Denver.
Celts looking for bigs to replace fallen Raef, but they've found their offense and, somehow, first place. Just in time for 'Toine's return.
Getting Ricky to feel at home is only the first big project. Celts have to start playing better at home, too: 8-8 won't get it done.
If there is an MVP candidate in the East, especially with Allen Iverson out, it has to be Paul Pierce, who's leading the league in fourth-quarter scoring and leading Celts in, well, everything.
As Coach Obie recently noted, Celts are on their third team since training camp started. So we'll give 'em a little more time to turn around a home record (8-10) that's getting worse, not better.
6-1 road record against the West and Welsch's progress are nice (and needed) diversions from the suddenly sad Vin Man situation.
C's have played more games than anyone else. Means they have less time than anyone to start playing better (and switch back to black sneaks) at home (10-13).

No one else in the league is .500 or better on the road (11-11) and sub-.500 at home (11-13). Throw in the success against the West (9-7) and the Vin Man situation and it's a confusing team to assess.

Even though the mandatory center selection of Big Z bumped him on our ballot, and no matter how much chaos Celts endure, Pierce will probably wind up in L.A. If so, consider it his consolation for a fast-fading season.

Since they're better on the road than at home, Celts might not mind that they don't have a home game until Feb. 25. But Ricky is bound to get the blame if Boston loses Monday, after 13 straight wins over Cavs.
Pierce lingered in East's locker room long after the All-Star defeat, probably because he can't be too geeked to be rejoining a blown-up Celtics team that lost to Chicago by 20 last Thursday.
Dream job? It's tough for Carroll to make that case, sporting a 1-11 record since taking over for Coach Obie, lowlighted by a 1-6 trip out West and that 22-0 deficit in Portland.

Ainge defenders (yes, there apparently are some) come out of the woodwork to argue that Brandon Hunter was equal value for Darius Songaila. Yet even John Carroll concedes it's too early to say C's know what they have in Hunter.

Truth be told, Ainge would undoubtedly prefer a lottery pick. But he has to be enjoying a 5-0 spurt almost as much as Coach Carroll, even if the opposition -- Minnesota aside -- has been on the weak side.
From 1-12, the worst start of any coach in Celtics history, Carroll is on a 7-2 roll and reports losing 16 pounds on the South Beach Diet. Committee's jealous.
Have to bring this up for no other reason besides the fact it's ESPN-related: John Carroll could easily work as Sal Paolantonio's twin or body double if this NBA coaching thing doesn't work out.
Pierce says: 'We're in, baby. We're in. Pencil us in.' Looking at Celts' remaining schedule, we can't really argue.
Don't expect them to apologize, but C's will be toting sub-.500 records at home and on the road into the playoffs if they get in. Viva Las East.
Just a hunch, but a team that just backed into the Least playoffs by losing four straight ain't going to upset Indiana this time. But we can still applaud Boston's rally from a 23-36 start.

den.summary: Since Premiere Week was all about ridiculous hype, let's overblow Nuggets' two wins and give 'Melo some deserved spotlight.
We concede: No. 12 spot might have been stretching it. But little No. 11 is still legit, just like Boykins was in Golden State.
Five wins and four games with at least 100 points? This early in Carmelo Era, Nuggets will take it.
Unless you consider NBA TV a national network -- and we don't because it's so damn hard to get -- Carmelo won't be on national TV again this season. More ROY motivation for Melo.

Even with Carmelo shooting just 38 percent, and even with Andre shooting more than he's passing, Nuggets have home wins over Spurs, Kings and Mavs. Even if it's just a hot start, that puts them alongside Utah atop the November Surprise standings.
Even with bad home loss to Boston, Nuggets are on pace to win their 18th game before Christmas and finish with -- huh? -- 53 victories. But, caution: The road beckons.
Staying in front of Grizz and Jazz, not Mavs and Spurs, is the realistic goal. Yet that'll be tough, too.
Don't have the Midwest lead any more, but Nuggets do have only one win less than last season's total. And a HIGHER RANKING THAN UTAH!
Of all the early surprise teams, like Memphis and Utah and Milwaukee, Nuggets have shown the most staying power. Not looking like such a fluke at 11-6 vs. West opposition.

Yet another Midwest upstart (a la Rockets and Grizz) that wasn't ready for the lofty reaches of the top seven. Nuggets slumped after promotion to top six and blew the chance to win 20 games by New Year's Day for first time since 1977.

Denver management would be the first to tell you this isn't the ninth-best team in the league. But who else belongs up here? The elite probably stops at No. 7 and the jumble goes from No. 8 down to the mid-teens.

5-7 stretch after a 19-11 start is a tad alarming ... until you remember that Nuggets still haven't lost three in a row ... and that Nuggets -- yes, Nuggets -- have made it past the 41-game pole as a top-10 squad.
Not sure why they want Quentin Richardson, with 'Melo doing just fine, but that's the story in circulation: Nugs targeting Q and his fist-tapping buddy D-Miles (to help lure Q) in free agency.
Houston, beware: For basically 50 games, the Nuggets have really looked like the team Phoenix was supposed to be: Sixth-best team in the West.
Check that: Nuggets, Grizz and Rockets have all been out of the playoffs too long to start thinking they're in. That's especially true for Denver, which is 10-12 since a 19-11 start.
Maybe they'd prefer to be West's eighth seed. Nuggets' karma from that spot is good, if memory serves.
In spite of bad losses at Orlando and Miami, the Nuggets move up one on the premise that the West's top eight is looking (dare we say) set.
Carmelo can't do much more to get Nuggets winning again: Only three players (T-Mac, Kobe and Iverson) had a higher scoring average in February than Anthony's 27.1 ppg.
The only thing to cheer up Nuggets these days is the way Portland is unraveling anew. Because it looks like Denver will need all the help it can get to hold onto the No. 8 spot.
With the way the Blazers are charging, and with the Jazz back over .500, routing Utah on Sunday night just might have been the win of the season for Kiki's Nuggets.

Realistic observers will forgive the young Nuggets if they miss the playoffs in the mighty West. But Anthony's sitdown and the subsequent sniping -- that stuff's got to stop immediately. That stuff can seriously take some shine off the season.
Forgive 'Melo for the 'quitter' incident. He can't do much more than he's doing to keep Denver in playoff hunt, having scored 25 points in all but four of 29 games in one recent stretch.
Nice response to a crisis: Five straight home wins, including a victory over Houston on Friday to clinch just their second 40-win season since 1994-95.
If Nuggets miss out, they'll have every reason to be brokenhearted. They're finishing pretty strong, judging by a six-game home winning streak ... in victories by a combined 83 points.

hou.summary: Instead of the bad -- Griffin-gate and a home loss to Grizz -- Rockets focus instead on rout of oft-mentioned Nugs and Yao's good start.
If first five games are true reading, Van Gundy has made immediate impact, especially defensively. Problem is, Houston has only played one sure playoff team so far.
To their credit, they're winning almost every game they're supposed to. But Rockets have yet to stage a real upset, and play seven of next nine on road after giveaway in Toronto.
Last two losses, at Toronto and at Portland, were fall-from-ahead jobs. Rockets better quit it if they want to hold off Phoenix to finish sixth in West.

Defensive numbers still look good for these Van Gundys, at No. 3 in points allowed (84.3) and No. 1 in opponent FG shooting (.386). Fact remains, though, that Houston has just two wins over teams with winning records.
Can no longer bust on Rockets for their shortage of quality wins. They had three this week to make a strong Team O' Week push.
As long as they hang onto a top-eight spot in the West, Rockets can live with being No. 3 in Texas for another season, as their trouble beating Spurs suggests.
Rockets must really think Van Gundy is an East Coast guy, because they're 7-10 vs. the West and 8-1 otherwise. And struggling to score no matter where the opposition hails from.
Rockets move up only by default, because their week wasn't the best apart from toppling the Lakers on ABC. But the East is making lots of Westerners look good these days.
We admitted last week that a top-seven slot is probably too high for these guys. Sounds like Jeff Van Gundy agrees with us.
Van Gundy needn't worry about being sent back to TNT, as he joked the other day. But in this West, as inconsistent as his Rockets are, missing the playoffs is a serious possibility.
For all the talk about what Yao can't do, wouldn't you want him on your team? Rhetorical question, because there's only one answer.
Yao is hushing doubters on a daily basis now. Houston's only real problem these days is the lack of success vs. West: 11-13.
Only thing consistent about Rockets is Van Gundy, after a year in TV, routinely breaking off genius quotes. The team? Every week it looks like a different team.

Houston certainly doesn't need to see Yao, on top of his long seasons and busy summers, playing in the Rookie Game AND the All-Star Game. The news, though, is mostly good this week: Francis, after all, did not attend the Pro Bowl.

You know we're good with Yao-za, but even rivals are pushing him to be more aggressive. Heard during the All-Star Game: KG yelling 'Dunk That!' at Yao after the big man caught a pass and opted for a short push shot.
Houston's now 13-2 when Yao scores at least 21, as he continues to make a case for All-NBA votes. Ditto for an All-Interview Team spot, with his very underrated sense of humor.

JVG is going to end Rockets' playoff drought, but the challenge then is avoiding a Texas team in the first round. Houston is 2-21 against San Antonio over the past six seasons, and has never beaten Dallas with Yao in the lineup.

They've been needing quality wins against Western opposition and just bagged two, beating Minny in Minny and halting their hex against Dallas by holding off Mavs at home. Does this mean we have a Terrific Ten, as opposed to an Elite Eight?

Now that the Rockets are starting to beat some good teams, too, it's safe to say that Texas will be sending all three of its teams to the playoffs for the first time since 1990. Actually, it's been safe to say that for a while now.
Outbursts from Stevie Franchise aside, Yao's Rockets still look like a pretty dangerous No. 7 seed that will be playing someone good in the first round: Minny or San Antonio, most likely.
Jeff Van Gundy has never had a losing season as a coach. He avoided it this season in spite of Rockets' 18-24 record vs. West foes, the worst of any playoff team.
Didn't exactly respond well to the promotion, did they? We've been saying all along Rockets are a lock to get in, but they're not in yet, after losing five of six and eight of 11.

The good news: Rockets have avoided that 'historic collapse' you've heard so much about. The bad news: Rockets probably lost their status as a dangerous first-round opponent by coming close to collapsing.

por.summary: Committee feels like another disappointed Portlander. Showed some rankings faith in Blazers, who promptly get outworked by Utah on Opening Night. Someone on that team owes us a meal at Jake's.
'Sheed-to-Dallas rumors over the weekend were bogus, but you can expect plenty more. 'Sheed is in last year of his deal, and this is slowly becoming Zach's team.

First-half showing against Sacto was deplorable, but the comeback was laudable. Cheeks deserved it for agreeing to keep his thankless job for another season ... even though, frankly, he deserves a longer extension.
I left Blazers here in spite of Golden State loss and latest Bonzi shenanigans because, honestly, there's no obvious No. 10 team in this league right now. Seriously. I'm open to suggestions.
Bonzi Wells was stripped of his co-captaincy ... and replaced by Damon Stoudamire. Nah, Blazers don't miss Pippen and Sabonis.
You knew Blazers would make a trade sooner rather than later ... but before they won a road game? Blazers and Cavs are only winless road teams.
For once, we're going to ignore Hurricane 'Sheed because we're still struggling to believe that Coach Cheeks was kicked out of a game a week ago. Apparently it IS contagious.
On the road, they've had nothing but trouble. At home, Blazers can't stay out of trouble. At least they're consistent.

Guess we shouldn't be surprised that Portland has a split personality, but it's still tough to explain beating the league's best road team on national TV (Wolves) and then falling to 0-10 on the road by losing in Cleveland.
Make that two records that boggle the mind, from a team that still has a fair bit of talent: Road record (1-11) and overall record (under .500 now).
Blazers didn't have 19 losses last season until Feb. 21. On the bright side, at least Blazers' problems are mostly basketball-related for once.

Here's your Biggest Disappointment Out West. Which is why it says here that Allen will ultimately be convinced that he has to trade 'Sheed before Feb. 19,  unless the owner (who rebuffed Dallas) wants to punt on the rest of the season.
They're the anti-Mavs at present, losing 10 of 12 and looking like they're waiting for a big trade. First-ever trip to the lottery beckons.
Players must believe that Paul Allen wants to keep 'Sheed for the rest of the season. Ever since the trade talks with Dallas collapsed, the Blazers look somewhat settled and even won a few roadies.
There's no question Randolph belongs in the All-Star Game on numbers alone. But if the Nuggets didn't get an All-Star, the Blazers weren't going to, either.
Portlanders wanted Bonzi and 'Sheed gone and got their wish. Of course, now they're stuck with the leftovers until the big roster restructuring in 2005.
If anyone in West's bottom six looks capable of nicking the No. 8 slot, it's Zach's team. (You're welcome, Utah).

It shouldn't surprise you that Miles is a catalyst with Blazers, compared to his minimal impact with Cleveland, because he's better when he can focus on D and restrict his offensive focus to chipping in.

Lose at home to Bonzi's Grizz, then lose at home to Sheed's Pistons, then lose by 20 on the road to Clips with Zach suspended. It's weeks like that which make Cheeks' return to Philly seem inevitable.
It's definitely still a three-team race for that last spot in the West playoffs, after Blazers dust the Wolves twice in five days and run their record vs. Sacto to 3-1.
Portland can deal with the loss in Indy, because Blazers won the season series from the other three division leaders: Jersey (2-0), Sacto (3-1) and Minny (3-1).
This ain't the East. No backing into a playoff spot in the West. Blazers, on a 7-2 run, only just moved into a tie for No. 8.

Besides the playoff streak, there's another streak on the line: Portland hasn't finished under .500 since going 39-43 in 1988-89. And losses at home to reeling Hornets don't help, with a rough schedule from here to the finish line.
Of course we considered Zach strongly for MIP. But his big improvement was seen in last spring's Dallas series; his outstanding play this season merely built on that jump.

gsw.summary: Even without Van Exel, Richardson and Murphy, stayed with Mavs and Lakers and throttled Philly. Bonus boost: Look for NVE back this week, earlier than expected.
Van Exel makes speedy return from minor knee surgery, so you'll see all the key Warriors save Murphy and Foyle in Wednesday's ESPN nightcap vs. Detroit.
A .500 start wasn't bad with half the team out injured, but home losses to Suns and Clips were ill-timed with Kings-Spurs-Rockets trip underway.
Van Exel hurried back from knee surgery in part to show people how ready he is to play for Warriors. GS has to hope that gesture didn't cause more damage.
Four-game win streak gives Warriors winning record to bring into December for first time since 1994-95. That season, incidentally, started Warriors' nine-year playoff drought, the league's longest.
Still .500 after two disappointing losses to Denver ... but in the midst of a heavy road stretch (13 out of 18 away) that won't be easy for an injury-hit squad.
Happy holidays: In only three games at home between now and New Year's, visitors will be Lakers, Kings and surging Celtics.
Road losses to Orlando and Miami are not acceptable for a team that prides itself on dominating Eastern Conference opposition. Especially in a week when Troy Murphy finally returns.
Another team we can't figure. Lose to Orlando and Miami after dominating East last season. Rebound by beating Lakers and Kings, powers that always trounce them. And yet still can't beat Denver.
Those back-to-back victories over Lakers and Kings were great ... but perhaps the Warriors didn't get the memo that the season lasts 82 games, not 27. They haven't won since.
Van Exel's relationship with Muss is getting all the attention, but Troy Murphy's ongoing injury struggles are the bigger worry for Warriors.
Scratch that. Murphy's ailments AND Van Exel's knee are both suddenly bigger issues than NVE's relationship with Coach Muss.
Van Exel and Muss weren't exactly harmonious, but Warriors would rather have a debate about who's the go-to guy rather than see Nick hobble away to IR.
There has been a bit more tension this season, compared to last season, but things could be a lot worse. The proof: Last year's Cinderella Warriors were 20-25 at same stage.
The look of pain on Uncle Cliffy's face, during that two-point quarter Sunday night, was the look of a guy who knows his career-long playoff streak is unavoidably slipping away.
No jinx here: Cardinal responds to his Cult Heroes nomination with a 32-point game last Wednesday. That's more points than Cardinal ever scored in any of his first three NBA seasons.
Would still be in the playoff race if not for a recent 1-14 road slide. Instead: Damp and Van Exel could be down to their last 28 games as Warriors.
It's losses like Saturday's, at lowly Chicago, that will cost Uncle Cliffy his playoff streak. Injuries have certainly hurt Warriors, but their 3-17 road slump is the killer.
Committee still believes that Warriors, had they been healthy, would have challenged for No. 8. But now Van Exel, to continue the injury trend, is probably done for the season.
Memo to Lawrence Frank: Unheralded, dimunitive coaches who rank as rookie sensations don't stay darlings forever. Just ask Muss.

The four-game win streak is nice, especially with two wins coming on national TV, but Warriors would need to win their last 13 games to have any shot at preventing a 10th straight season out of the playoffs.

We were just kidding when we suggested Warriors should try to finish the season with 17 straight wins, but they're apparently going for it anyway. Muss might be in trouble, rightly or wrongly, but he can definitely coach.
Besides injuries, what ruined Warriors' season is their inability to dominate the East like they did last season. They went only 14-16 against the East in 2003-04, compared to 19-11 in '02-03.

Injuries and controversies submarined these guys again, but facts is facts: As Denver closes in on halting its eight-season playoff drought, Golden State stretched its drought to a league-high 10 straight seasons, despite this current 11-4 spurt.

tor.summary: You want insane? After Vinsanity goes for 65 points in first two games ... Raps manage just 56 as a team in game No. 3.
Actually, Raps will need more than a healthy Vince if they hope to regularly score 80 points. But credit O'Neill for the immediate improvement on D.
Only mistake from Vince in comeback was questioning Bosh selection. Kid is helping VC more than any other Raptor.
If they can't get Jalen and Donyell, Raps will have to keep probing until they get someone else. Unless Raps want to score less than 70 points 25 times in 82 games. That's their current pace.
Rose better bloom quickly in his new city. Raps gave up a huge fan favorite to finally make the deal happen, and departures of Antonio and JYD (the fans' guy) put more immediate pressure on Bosh.
Had some competition for Team O' Week from Grizz, Rockets, Wolves -- and Lakers, obviously -- but Raps had to be the ones, scoring 92 or more in all four games since big trade.
Raps drop two straight to halt the honeymoon before the schedule starts really getting hard. Next two are at Dallas and at San Antonio.
We warned you not to get too geeked up about the 5-0 start post-trade. Last six games (1-5) prove committee right yet again.
Trade update: Raps were 8-8 before getting Jalen and Donyell, and are 7-6 since. At least they're no longer winless on the road vs. West, beating Clips on Sunday to go to 1-7.
No question Jalen and Donyell have made a difference in T-Dot, but don't forget the other new power forward: 6-foot-5 Michael Curry, who is willing to guard anyone. Or at least try.
The good news: Raps have won five of seven. The bad news: "Improved" offense has cracked 90 only once in that span.
Up one by default ... because Raps won't be able to say they're one of East's (six) teams over .500 for much longer if Vince sits much longer.
This just in: Raps apparently not quite the same squad when Vinsanity is unavailable. To date: Raps are 20-51 all time when VC is out.
Just 1-4 since Vince's return. Worse yet, Raps so easily could have been 3-2. Last two losses, to Pistons and Lakers, came by a total of two points. Ouch.
You know it's tough filling out the top 20 when Raps, in the midst of a 3-9 slump and after losing Bosh, move up a few.
With Jalen out, Raps need a spark. Maybe Raps got one Sunday when Vince got only 16 minutes of PT from Indy's Carlisle.
Fearless prediction: Without Vince and Jalen, Raps probably aren't going to last in the East's top eight. We know it's scant consolation, but Toronto still has the best street hot dogs in the league.
On Jan. 11, Raps were 19-16. Boston was 20-16 on the same morning. Back-to-back losses to Celts mean injury-ravaged Raps are 6-18 since, compared to Boston's 5-17.
Raps have thrown themselves a lifeline with wins over Heat and Hornets. But they still look like the team most likely to drop out of the East's top eight.
As bad as things got for a while, with 13 losses in 15 games, this is the East. So ... with Jalen back early and Rod Strickland added on, Raps ain't out of it yet.
Let's be honest: Vince could easily have won Line O' The Week with that 42-6-12 vs. Hornets to keep Toronto alive.
Vince scores 40 twice in one week ... and no one notices with both coach and GM in danger of losing their jobs.

In Grunwald's defense, this would have been a decent team -- by East standards, we stress -- had it avoided injury. Vince, Bosh, Jalen and Donyell (by East standards, remember) ain't the worst foursome ... but it ain't the healthiest, either.
An ugly second half just gets uglier: Toronto has lost six straight at home, 10 of 11 overall and now faces the shame of a 50-loss season.

phi.summary: Big Dog returns from suspension this week to start life as AI's trusted companion. Doubtful that the Dog helps Ayers' leaky defense, though.
It's up to Iverson to help Big Dog get established, but facts is facts: AI has started season in top gear.
AI is scorching, going for 36 or more three times in four games, but we're fairly sure Sixers won't go far if Big Dog plays in less than half the games.
Have Sixers been healthy since the '01 Finals? Doesn't seem like it ... and come to think of it, they weren't healthy then, either.

All in all, AI has to be happy with things, in spite of a 12-point game in Indy and a $10,000 fine for his one-finger salute in Milwaukee. A win over Larry Brown and a 50-point game vs. Atlanta more than evened things out.
Considering all the injuries, Sixers will take first in Atlantic no matter how average their record is. Especially since Nets might finally be awakening.
Tough to get excited about Big Dog's long-awaited return when AI misses two games in one week. Which never happens.
Sixers are 25-36 all-time without Iverson and it's tough to see that record getting better with all their other hobbled personnel.
We interrupt this Iverson injury panic to ask: If Kyle Korver can't get his shot off in the pros, as some scouts suggested, how is he shooting 56 percent on 3-pointers in December?
Ledger now reads 27-40 all-time without Allen Iverson, and 3-7 during Answer's latest absence, even including upset of Spurs. So, yeah. They'll be glad to have him back this week.

AI isn't happy with the big-name local radio host, but he can't have any quarrel with the league office after suspensions enabled the Sixers to play the Clips without Maggette and the Nets without K-Mart in back-to-back games.
Big Dog starting to score. Now if Sixers can get AI and Big Dog scoring simultaneously, that should secure a playoff berth.
Everyone's getting a bit testy in Philly, after five losses in six games and four straight losses when Iverson scores 30.

Billy King has insisted Ayers isn't in trouble, but it'll be interesting to see how Sixers react if Cheeks -- the guy they wanted -- comes onto the market. And with a good Philly guy (Jim O'Brien) already available.
Lost 34 games all of last season. Just lost by 30 points to a Boston team that hadn't won under John Carroll. Chances are this 4-11 slide gets worse.
Chris Ford is the first ever to coach Celtics and 76ers, and not a moment too soon. Trading McKie for JYD's energy and board work won't hurt, either.
Ford did what Ayers should have done, especially with little shot at keeping the job long-term. Ford took a hard line with AI to try to keep the rest of the team in line.
Can beating Minny save Philly's season? It's more likely AI sets a new single-season career mark for games missed; he's at 18 and his previous worst was 22 games ('01-02).

Are we all in agreement now that Sixers will be the first of the six Sub-.500 Playoff Hopefuls to be eliminated from the race? It sounds like even AI agrees: "This might be the worst season that I've had since I've been a Sixer."
Chris Ford is showing interim coaches everywhere how it's done. Coach like you have nothing to lose -- don't coddle the star -- because chances are someone else will get the job long-term anyway.
Not quite crumbling like the Vet, but Sixers just tacked a four-game skid onto their, uh, unexpected 6-2 record when both Iverson and Big Dog are unavailable through injury.
Does anyone else see Sixers' recent success with AI in street clothes as a message from the other players that they, too, want to sample life with AI in another city?

Back-to-back home losses, after routing Golden State, seem to have hushed the Better Without Allen talk. Worse yet, only one player (Willie Green) has scored more than 18 points in the past four games -- Green had 22 on April Fool's Day.

They're coming at Iverson from all angles now. Besides the heat he's getting in Philly, neighboring New Jersey rubbed more salt into AI's grill by bringing J-Kidd and K-Mart off the bench in their first games back from injury, a la Timmy Duncan.

orl.summary: It has to be at least a little disconcerting that, counting preseason games, Orlando still hasn't won a home game in five attempts.
Came so close to 2-0 start ... but now Magic is 0-5 at home with five-game trip looming. Doc will have to start winning eventually.

Only solace for Magic fans: Last time they had a team that lost six straight at home, it led to 18-64 record that begat Shaq in 1992 draft. Then again ... there aren't many Shaqs in the draft anymore.
Yes, it gets worse. The proof: So much for the notion that signing Olowokandi, struggling with his health and game in Minny, would have changed things.
Look on most Magic faces suggest they don't believe a win is coming. Grant Hill, meanwhile, says he wants to come back in February, whether it helps or not.
More coaches than wins this season. Not a single win yet in November and December. The cold, hard facts are piling up fast.
Johnny Davis was on the Cleveland team that started 2-19 in 1984-85 ... and still made the playoffs. No wonder he's always so upbeat.
Not trying to take anything away from Magic, just telling the truth: Teams probably aren't as focused when they play Orlando now that the streak is over. Credit Magic for taking advantage, though.
In theory, yes, Orlando is still in playoff contention. Reality, however, reminds us that the Magic is 3-12 at home, after 26-15 last season.
With a 1-5 slump and an hobbling/vanishing T-Mac, Magic suddenly only a .500 team (7-7) since halting its 19-game freefall.
Don't ask us to explain A) how Magic still has more road wins (five) than home wins (four) and B) how Magic moved up this week.
After eight straight road losses, Magic has chance to lose 15th home game -- matching last season's total -- against Milwaukee on Monday. Good seats still available.
It can't help Magic's outlook to see D. Armstrong, a guy they drove out of town, carry Hornets to a victory in San Antonio without Baron and Mash.
We repeat: All-Star voting is not Who's The Best Player? It's: Who Had The Best First Half? Hence, our contention that T-Mac, unable to prevent a 19-game skid early on, shouldn't be a starter.

Even if most experts agree that T-Mac hasn't played as well as he can, no one wants to see the kid continue to struggle with back trouble. Especially not with a franchise that has already endured the Grant Hill saga.
After T-Mac spearheads a $72,000 charity drive Sunday, let's wish for some good things to happen to a good guy in the second half. He has suffered enough.
It's a big jump, agreed, but the Magic entertained us with T-Mac's placekick and punt ... and multiple wins and trades.
The hits just keep coming: 4-2 in last six games, but both losses came in OT. Then there's this: T-Mac is talking louder than ever about his opt-out.
Instead of a late-season cameo from Grant Hill, now it sounds as though Hill might elect to keep sitting ... and that T-Mac's back might put him in street clothes for a spell.

Orlando can only hope that having a hockey guy in charge (Weisbrod) works out like it did in Jersey (Lamoriello) ... although, truth be told, Thorn and Kidd (and, yes, Lord Byron) had a lot more to do with Nets' success than Lou.
With Chicago winning two in a row, Magic's lead in the race for the most Ping Pong balls is up to 2 1/2 games.
Committee's boss says we have to do 29 of these a week. We're open to suggestions to keep it fresh down here.

Orlando crashes through our writer's block with 10 straight losses, seven in a row in one stretch by at least 15 points. That's a new NBA record, and not exactly the best campaign to support Magic's increase in ticket prices for next season.

The most popular suggestion in response to our plea for help with Magic comments: Put the Bobcats at No. 29. As a farewell, at least this week we can talk about Orlando clinching the most Ping-Pong balls.

mil.summary: Never expected Bucks climbing this high, but they deserve it after ousting Indiana and embarrassing Chicago. And after T.J. Ford made a run at debuting with a triple-double.
Four good wins and not a bad loss yet for the rookie coach. Porter's young Bucks have only been beaten by Wolves, Pistons, Lakers.
Lost the big grudge-match game against Flip Murray's Sonics but get this: Coach Porter is still undefeated (3-0) in the second game of back-to-backs.
Practicing 5-on-6 isn't helping T.J. Ford's shot (32 percent), but it's helping the rest of the Bucks' offense. Toronto win moved Milwaukee to a very respectable 3-4 in road games.
.500 records in the East are so scarce that you have to laud Bucks for winning half their games in Month 1. Only five East teams did.
No one can explain how Bucks are 1-5 in first night of back-to-backs, and 5-1 on second night, but overall record still looks better than us smart guys predicted.
Bucks continue to contend for a top-five spot in the Overachiever Standings, too. Staying up there will be tough, though, if Kukoc and Skinner don't heal soon.
If it's up to us, Michael Redd is an All-Star. Sadly, it's not up to us, so we can't promise anything.
More Michael Redd propaganda: 20 points or better in 19 of last 25 games. Team propaganda: Bucks on a 6-3 uptick.
Eleven times this season, Bucks have been right at .500. About eight or nine times more than expected, in other words.
Forget the loss at MSG. Bucks have won eight straight at home, with some quality victims on that list: New Jersey, Detroit, Indiana and Dallas.
No shame losing that home win streak to scorching Pistons. Bucks generally still beating the teams they can reasonably expect to beat, at 17-9 vs. East foes.
Not that we're running out of Redd propaganda -- he just had a 40-pointer, after all -- but there's apparently a whole team in Milwaukee, judging by Bucks' 46-36 pace..
Couldn't maintain the momentum after big Spurs conquest, but the Bucks' little 14-1 run at home clinches their top-10 debut.
Top-10 status was short-lived, but the Bucks know that, eventually, they're going to have to win a few roadies if they want to stay where they are, here and in the standings.
Playing in a smaller market, with less pressure, should help Van Horn immensely. Another score for Larry Harris, whose unheralded squad has East's second-best home record (20-6) behind Indy (21-5).
Finally halted a long road losing streak. Unfortunately, that tough defense Coach Porter demands has gone missing.

March is massive for our man Redd and Co. Road-challenged Bucks play nine of the month's first 13 games away, including trips to Sacto and Lakers ... and with an Indy home-and-home looming to cap the month.
Milwaukee has a real opportunity to claim the No. 4 seed, with Hornets stumbling and four of its next five games at home. But the Bucks are mired in their own 7-9 malaise.

Milwaukee needs home-court advantage in the first round to get out of the first round, but this 8-12 swoon (1-5 in the last six) means Bucks might have wasted a prime opportunity to gain ground on the Hornets.

The T.J. Ford-less slide is so pronounced now (1-8) that the East is down to four teams with records of .500 or better. And Milwaukee's remaining schedule is such that a sub-.500 finish might be unavoidable.
T.J. Ford might not even be back for the playoffs? Van Horn turns an ankle? One of the fairy tales of the season gets sadder by the day.

Here's another team, like gutty Denver, that showed us something when it had to. Bucks won the season series from Indy, finished the week with three wins and gave themselves hope of hanging onto No. 4 in the East. All while shorthanded.
Since the 16-team playoff format was adopted in 1983-84, no No. 4 seed has ever had a winning percentage below .524. Bucks have to win their final two games just to get to .524.

cle.summary: What did you expect from Le Cavs on a Sacramento-Phoenix-Portland trip? They stay top 20 because LeBron has exceeded all expectations to date.
If you want to know why Cavs consider D-Miles to be key to their season, Saturday was Exhibit A. Miles goes for career-best 26 points and Cavs finally win one, beating Wiz.
If Silas can make a player out of Diop, who has helped matters by losing a lot of weight, there must be hope for Silas getting Ricky Ricky to play the right way.
On top of all the turmoil, Cavs suddenly missing Dajuan. He'd be starting in Miles' place if healthy, and now Ricky looks like odd man out with Cavs, not Wagner.
Amazing as it is to see LeBron at No. 2 in the league in minutes already -- so much for bringing the kid along slowly -- it's tough to focus on any other stat beyond those 31 straight road losses.
Boozer's back, and there's more good news: Next road game isn't until Dec. 15.
There's an interesting little race brewing. Let's see what happens first for Cavs: trading Ricky Davis or winning on the road.
Since Ricky's departure, LeBron is more aggressive, energetic, focused and intense in the locker room. And -- get this -- 2-1 on the road.
Cavs now up to 6-8 when LeBron scores at least 20, which has happened in seven out of Cleveland's last 10 games. Yeah, the trade is working so far.
Imminent return of Wagner and Diop should at least muffle the constant trade speculation swirling around Big Z and D-Miles. OK, probably not.
Nineteen road games ... 14 sellouts ... two victories. Numbers that don't help LBJ's ROY campaign when Carmelo's Nuggets are 14-9 vs. the West.
Ankle injury, like Cavs' road woes, doesn't change our belief: East coaches will vote LeBron in as an All-Star because they all already agree that Rookie Game isn't suitable for his game.
Miles will be remembered fondly for at least one contribution ... as one of the anchors on the team bad enough to land LeBron in the draft.
Lookie here: Cavs up to 12-11 since Ricky Davis' exile after LeBron's 38-pointer. I'm gullible enough to say they're still in the playoff hunt.
Make that 13-14 since Ricky Davis' exile. If Cavs are serious about challenging for the No. 8 slot, they simply can't lose home games like Saturday's against Washington.
As entertaining as East was, we still say that game needed LeBron (and 'Melo).  But Cavs have more pressing concerns: LBJ averaged just 15 ppg on 32-percent shooting in four games before the break.
James Gang just won two games -- home to Spurs, and at Knicks -- to make up for two of their many blown leads. If Cavs can extend the new trend, No. 8 is legitimately within reach.
Silas wasn't lying when he said (repeatedly) in October that his teams do better in the second half. For his career, he has an 88-50 record after the All-Star break, compared to 122-127 beforehand.
Committee didn't have nice things to say about the McInnis acquisition, but facts is facts: Cavs' new PG has a sparkling 67 assists against eight turnovers in the past seven games.

Updating a stat that wasn't properly explained the first time it appeared: Since taking over Hornets in 1999-2000, Silas is 94-51 after the All-Star break and 122-127 before it. As Silas predicted in October, Cavs are upholding that trend.
