More data to please McInnis fans: Cleveland is 17-8 with him and 0-2 when he's out injured. Cavs need him back in a hurry, too, because they're not in the playoffs yet.
Credit where credit is due: Cavs are 17-9 when McInnis plays ... and 15-31 without him.

Savior McInnis should be back Tuesday, but now the other veteran integral to the turnaround (Eric Williams) is out. Maybe Cleveland can draw inspiration from the commericial: 'You're wearing a Cavs jersey, you don't give up.'

The playoffs would have been better with LeBron in them, given his 22-5-6 averages since the All-Star break. You suspect he would have made it had Cavs not needed half a season to get the roster tweaked to suit him.

mem.summary: Grizz feasted on East last season. So, curiously, they lost home opener to Boston and then won at Houston.
As good as Pau looked at Eurobasket 2003, you expected better production from him. Of course, I also expected Hubie to play him more than 29.7 mpg.
Great timing. Team O' Week next plays in Wednesday's ESPN date with Detroit. Eager to see how real Grizz is after a few nice wins.
Only losses in last six: Detroit at home, Lakers (big) on the road. Guess I have to give Hubie's platoon system a chance, even though I still don't like it.

Comeback in Cleveland, with assist from Cavs, showed some grit. The rest of their week -- big loss in Sacto, home loss to struggling Minny -- showed that our hesitation about last week's promotion was justified.
Six road wins already after just eight in each of past two seasons. Plus West has ammo (Swift, Battier) to make another trade before February.

After all those sappy stories about Hubie and J-Will ... what if Grizz is actually better with Earl Watson and Mike Miller running the point? Not that Memphis minds the confusion, reveling in what must be its first-ever taste of the top 10.

Honestly, I don't know how the computer allowed the Grizz up here. Hubie, meanwhile, gets points for honesty, but I'm not so sure it's smart to say publicly that a team is playing 10 guys instead of eight to build up everyone's trade value.
Unprecedented bump up to No. 7 might have made all the Grizz dizzy. They'll be safer placed here, and we're guessing Grizz can live with being this high.
Maybe no stat reflects how much tougher today's West compares to the 2002-03 West than this one: Grizz started 0-13 last season.
So which is more unlikely: Memphis getting snowed out of two straight games ... or Memphis sitting at .500 nearly halfway through the schedule, but still sitting in last place in the Midwest?
Every Midwest team belongs in top-10 range when every Midwest team is at least three games over .500. And the best might be forthcoming for Grizz, who play 24 of their final 43 games at home.
Best of the rest? Grizz can certainly make the argument after passing up Nuggets, Bucks and Jazz on Surprise Team-O-Meter.
Grizz, Rockets and Nuggets must be relieved Harpring is out, because that injury could be the difference in determining which one of these four teams misses out on the playoffs.
After 50 games, and more wins than any other season in franchise history, you'd have to say these guys are for real. With some separation now from Utah, the Grizz can really start dreaming playoffs.
When you realize Grizz is 11-9 against the rest of the top 10, it's clear. Grizz is Best O' The Rest entering the stretch run.
It doesn't quite have the ring of Elite Eight, but Grizz is leaving us no choice. Looks like we have an Elite Nine now, with Memphis assembling a 16-4 surge.
How unexpected is Grizz's rise to the brink of the Elite Eight? Franchise record for winning percentage, before this season, was .341. Nowadays they're flirting with .600.

With a 24-7 record since Jan. 1, and needing only four more wins to clinch their first winning season EVER, Grizz are making it very, very tough to keep them out of the top eight. We simply couldn't figure out which team to drop out.
Hubie is going to make it tough on Sloan, Porter, Adelman, Carlisle, Silas and any other COY hopefuls if Grizz really get to 51 wins, as their pace suggests.
Memphis is so deep that it can handle Indy without needing its Indiana native Bonzi. Good response to the Seattle slip-up.
You want to hear something really scary? Grizz can still WIN the Midwest, with two games left against Minny and already holding the tiebreaker over Spurs.
Before Hubie, Grizz had never won more than 10 road games in a season. Before Grizz, Hubie had only won 50 games once, in 1979-80 with Atlanta.

Committee could not ignore Sloan's coaching, but Hubie made an equally compelling case ... especially when you realize the Grizz's all-time winning percentage before this season wasn't too far over the Mendoza Line at .244.

okc.summary: Losing Ray for 6-8 weeks is a killer blow. At least Rashard's 50-pointer and Ronald Murray's storybook first two starts (46 points) softened the blow.
Blew chance to go 4-0, and now head East for four roadies. The good news: Ronald Murray continues to be Surprise O' The Season.
Why was MJ watching Bulls-Sonics? Why else? He wanted a first-hand glimpse of Flip Murray, too.
Thank you, again, Sonics. Even with Flip Murray climbing to fourth (FOURTH!) in league in scoring at 24.2 ppg, cozy home stretch opens with two poor losses (and nearly three in a row).

Flip Fever hit a lull this week when the Sonics suffered heavy losses to Nets and Jazz and rumblings started bubbling about ball movement. Murray came off the bench for first time all season in Saturday's win over Houston.
Flip Fever has cooled considerably and now our ESPN.com contributor Frank Hughes reports discord between McMillan and management. Ray Allen can't return soon enough.

Payton's place is in L.A. now, yet it seems as though Sonics are still awash in tension. We're also not quite clear how glue guy Brent Barry became 'expendable,' as the committee keeps reading elsewhere.
A 2-7 slide dropped Sonics two games under .500 for first time all season. That's why Denver win pumped them up so much. That and the Richie Frahm phenomenon.
Sonics glad to have Ray Allen back, even if it does crowd their backcourt. Ray makes more plays in Seattle than he ever did in Milwaukee.
You can pardon a rout in Sacto when you remember Sonics A) have Ray A. back, B) spoiled GP's return and C) are tied with SA with second-best road record in West (8-7).
Much as Seattle enjoyed Flip Fever, we're guessing Sonic Nation doesn't mind so much that no one's even talking about the Flipster anymore, now that Ray has hauled the Supes back over .500.
Seattle fans think we have it in for Supes. Only thing that really bugs us about Supes is how they go into a tailspin every time we move them up the ladder.
Here's another chance for Supes to prove us wrong, as we inch them closer to top 10 yet again. I'm listening, Seattle: Is another immediate drop inevitable?
Coach McMillan invites 10 media types to submit their preferred starting lineups. So that makes 11 people desperately missing Brent Barry and wondering where November's Flip Murray went.
First, a Ray Allen injury scare. Then a loss to end their mastery over Blazers. Moved up only because so many neighbors in this region are struggling.
Tough to be optimistic in the land of java, with the beloved Brent Barry on the trading block and 17 of Seattle's remaining 30 games on the road.
Injuries and size issues haven't stopped Sonics from hovering around .500 ... but that near-.500 record won't keep Nate off the list of Endangered Coaches, either.
Make that two things Seattle needs besides a dependable big man: Brent Barry (5-11 without him) and more games against Houston (Sonics are 3-0 vs. Rockets).
Safe to say Sonics' playoff fantasies have been extinguished. It's hard to say why they've fared better without Ray Allen in the lineup than they've fared without Brent Barry.
Does anyone remember Sonics' 6-2 start? Does anyone doubt we're going to use this line again before the season ends?
With our man Barry back and firing, Sonics prevent us from trotting out the 6-2 start line again by winning five straight, one more than Golden State on the list of too-late win streaks.
Seattle stretched its too-late win streak to seven games before finally losing to Portland. So we still have to hold off on the quips about that 6-2 start.
One reason Coach Nate is frustrated is because he's not used to losing. Sonics have secured their first consecutive sub-.500 seasons since racking up three in a row from 1984-85 through '86-87.
It sounds like Sonics don't want to fire Nate after an injury-filled season, but it also sounds like Nate doesn't really want to stay.

uta.summary: Lots of Nugget mentions in these rankings. Here's another: Jazz reminds you of last season's Nuggets with its gritty play and unheralded roster.
How reliable is Coach Sloan? Not only is Jazz making me (and millions) look stupid again, but Elias Sports Bureau says there have been 157 coaching changes since Sloan started in 1988.
More bad news for Doc Rivers: Sloan's stubborn Jazz is unbeaten at home and Monday's schedule calls for Orlando at Utah.

Now to see if Jazz can handle playing without the irreplaceable John Stock ... er, Carlos Arroyo. So far Jazz no-names have handled more games (5-4) against West teams than anyone besides Dallas (7-2).

We've been looking for a legit No. 10 team. Not picking Jerry Sloan's kids to stay up here, but Utah legitimately cracks top 10 for now with wins over several No. 10 wannabes: Minnesota (twice), Houston, Portland, Phoenix and Seattle.
Sloan probably isn't surprised Mailman missed first reunion via suspension. Only four of 11 games Malone has missed in his career were due to injury.
Took advantage of Iverson's absence to start a tough trip with a win at Philly. If Jazz is still over .500 after the five road games that follow, no one will be able to call them flukey.

Our poor pal Frank Hughes can't go anywhere without someone bringing up his prediction that Jazz would only win nine games. Fact is, the only thing 'worst' about this scrappy bunch is Kirilenko's haircut, which makes Steve Nash look stylin'.
Eighteen straight winning seasons is the NBA's longest current streak. You still willing to bet against Sloan making it 19?
This just in: As good as Sloan is, Jazz ain't gonna win without Mailman and Stockton and Harpring, who's now ailing.
The challenges keep coming at Sloan, professionally (Harpring's forthcoming surgery) and personally (his wife's bout with cancer). Sloan being Sloan, he accepts every challenge.
Who's the muppet who said the winning would stop now that Harpring has been shelved for the season? Doh.
Maybe the muppet knew what he was talking about. Or maybe what we should have written is that there's no way Jazz can lose Harpring AND Kirilenko after losing Stockton-to-Malone.
Didn't score 90 points once -- or win once -- in four games without Kirilenko. Since he came back, Jazz is shocking folks anew.
We know what you're thinking, Utahns. You want us to write Jazz off one more time, so a winning streak kicks in.
OK, Utahns, let's see if this works for you: Jazz's fade from playoff contention looks a certainty now, without Harpring and with 17 of the final 28 games on the road.
We're doing our part by dismissing Utah every week, but facts are facts: Jazz needed Googs and Giricek so much because it has been held under 100 points for 22 straight games.
You're welcome, Utahns. Looks like our latest write-off did the trick, judging by the recent 4-1 uptick.
This is unacceptable, Utah. A sub-.500 record? In the Midwest Division? This just won't do.
Why Sloan might be the COY whether or not the Jazz makes the playoffs: Utah starters make less than $5 million ... combined. The league's AVERAGE salary, remember, is $5 million.

The sense that the committee is starting to get from other voters is that it might not matter if Utah makes the playoffs when it comes to Sloan's COY candidacy. He might win no matter what happens from here.
Committee knows it's not supposed to be rooting for one team over another ... but how can you not root for Jerry and the Jazz to make the Elite Eight?

To secure a 19th straight winning season, whether it makes the playoffs or not, Jazz just needs a 3-3 finish. But it's no lock, with roadies against Mavs and Wolves and home dates with Grizz and Rockets remaining.
Utah ain't exactly finishing meekly, either. To keep pace with the Nuggets, Utah has held 38 of its past 40 opponents under 100 points.

was.summary: Moved up a spot just for what they did to Bulls. Yet offense is clearly lacking without Stack.
Still no hint of a Kwame breakout, but Jarvis Hayes is a rookie surprise and Wiz kids looked good beating Dallas.
Instead of that playoff guarantee from Arenas, Wiz would have preferred hearing him pledge to hold his temper. Outbursts temper excitement surrounding Arenas' otherwise quality start.
Wiz is lucky divisions were realigned only now. Had the plans for that cushy new Southeast Division been revealed in April, MJ might have never retired.
So moved by Wiz comeback attempt in Seattle, Coach Jordan is said to have been near tears. Touching story, but it'll be full-blown bawling if he has to go for a long stretch without Arenas and Stack.
All it took to halt losing streak was a 23-point fourth quarter from Larry Hughes. In other words, yes, they still need Arenas and Stack back.
Yet again we can say Wiz would have preferred a guarantee from Arenas that A) he'd be healthy and B) he wouldn't get ejected from games when he's out injured.

Still no Stack. Still no Arenas -- not a totally healthy Arenas, anyway. But things can't be all bad: I heard a new St. Louis song the other day pumping up Larry Hughes, along with Cleveland's D-Miles.
Kwame Brown isn't doing much scoring or rebounding. On top of all Wizards' other problems, Kwame has just two double-doubles all season.
Ugh: Arenas sits out 14 of 15, during which Wiz go 3-12 ... and then gets benched by Coach Jordan in third game back, spoiling Kwame's third double-double of the season.

Still only team in the league that hasn't shot 50 percent in a single game this season, and still no idea when Arenas and Stack will get to play together. Not the sort of consistency Wiz was hoping for.

Commemorated Lenny Wilkens Week by defeating Sonics in a rematch of yesteryear's Finals. More importantly, after 38 games of shooting less than 50 percent, Wiz has finally done that, too, avoiding sole possession of the NBA record by one game.
It's not like getting Webber or Mash back, because the season is already lost, but Coach Jordan is praying -- for his own sanity -- that Stack and Arenas really return after All-Star Weekend.
On cue: Stack is back ... and Kwame suffers a broken nose in warmups. Eddie Jordan must be wondering if his last name carries curse properties in D.C.
Give them a healthy Stack and Arenas and a contribution from Kwame and there just might be a team there. Wiz even ended a road drought of 11 games.
Even though one of their main three is always injured -- this time it's Hughes -- there's a hint of hope now with Stack back alongside Arenas and Kwame averaging 14 and 9 since Jan. 1.
Didn't see Mariah or anyone else remotely that slinky wearing a Wizards dress at All-Star Weekend this year. Thanks a lot, Mike.
Arenas and Brown better keep clashing, because it's the only thing worth watching with Wiz after the latest injury downer (Stack).
It only netted a 2-2 week, but Arenas can't do much more, averaging a tidy 30.8 ppg, 6.3 rpg and 6.3 apg in those games.

In this injury-filled, loss-filled season, perhaps nothing makes for more painful reading than the following: Wiz is an unfathomably woeful 1-17 against fellow Atlantic Division tenants. That's the worst division in basketball, in case you had forgotten.
It's been so long since our man DA has seen good ball up close; Wiz has endured six straight losing seasons and 15 in the last 17 seasons.
As Kwame plummets back to Earth, here's some rare good news: Arenas ranks second in the league in triple-doubles this season, with three to J-Kidd's nine.

As if Washington doesn't have enough regrets over the past 20 years, someone will inevitably point out next Monday in Detroit that Wiz used to have both public defenders from Wallace and Wallace before Pistons ever tried the concept.

Very quietly, Wiz won two out of three games against Atlantic foes in the past week to avoid tying the 1996-97 Celts (1-23) for a thoroughly unwanted record. And after this injury-filled season, Wiz will take it.

chi.summary: Omens for winning more than three road games this season ain't good after Chicago loses first roadie to Milwaukee ... by 30. To go with 25-point loss to Wiz in home opener.
Cartwright needs to be more stern with this group, if he wants to stay with this group. On the flip side, Bulls are up to 2-1 on the road, compared to last season's 3-38.
Cartwright was right to heed critics and put his foot down with Rose and Crawford, but there's a new issue: Ever-quirky Bulls are suddenly better on the road (3-1) than at home (1-6).
If trade with Toronto doesn't go down, secret hope might be that someone else out there makes a better offer for Rose, seeing how available he is. Always good to dream.
Skiles is fifth coach in two-plus seasons for Curry and Chandler. Let's hope fifth is the charm, because Chicago now has vets (Antonio and JYD) to play in the Baby Bulls' places.
Besides seeing Raptors take off since trade, Bulls also have to stomach all they gave up to get Jalen: Ron Artest, Brad Miller, Kevin Ollie.
Have we seen the last of Scottie Pip? Skiles, at 2-4, has plenty of problems to solve before even tackling that one.
Skiles is 3-6 since taking over, but it's difficult to get too optimistic when Bulls are without Curry, Chandler and Pippen (in addition to Jay Williams).
Benched on Monday, 30 points on Friday, 42 points on Saturday. Nice turnaround from Jamal Crawford, but we shouldn't be too surprised. He's scoring 20.9 ppg in December.
It's getting harder for us to believe in Eddy Curry's upside when he misses seven games and brings back a lot more than seven extra pounds upon his return. He's over 300 again.

Hiring of Skiles (8-13) can't be fairly judged for a while, but even John Paxson would tell you now that he wishes he hadn't cut Trenton Hassell in training camp to keep Linton Johnson ... who has since been cut as well.
Dare we say Bulls already have Biggest Disappointment in the East sewn up, because at least Orlando has the Grant Hill alibi.
At 9-19 under Skiles, the Bulls are inverse of the Grizz. And Nuggets. And Bucks. They're a wrong-way Surprise Team.
Before Skiles (9-23) has to start worrying about his job security, it sounds like Pippen (retirement) and Curry (career spasms) will precede him out the door. Shambolic.
John Paxson announced that Eddy Curry is not available, but one interested GM we spoke with says Curry was never really available even when teams thought he was.
Don't know why it's always Chicago, but Bulls have left us at a loss for words yet again.
Don't know why it's always Chicago, but the Bulls have left us at a loss for words one more time.
Just clinched their sixth straight losing season ... to end our two-week originality drought in this space.
We could (and should) say something nice about Kirk Hinrich's solid rookie season under the radar. Can't say anything nicer at this stage.
Curry is in the midst of his customary second-half tease ... only this time Skiles points out that the tease is all points-based and includes precious little defense and rebounding.

This shouldn't come as a surprise: Bulls are about to be tied for fifth on the list of consecutive 50-loss seasons with five. Clips hold the league record with 10. But there is good news: Chicago's off the bottom for the first time in five weeks.
Lakers are suddenly so hot that even a recent Lakers castoff -- Jannero Pargo -- can score 34 points for Chicago in his third game as a Bull.
A few weeks ago, MJ and Pip and Phil and HoGrant and Pax and who knows who else had a secret reunion behind closed doors at a Lakers-Bulls game in Chicago. Us? We miss Ray Clay.
Who has time to miss MJ when a whole season is spent pining for Ron Artest, Brad Miller and Elton Brand? Trenton Hassell, even.

nyk.summary: You applaud Houston for returning quickly from knee surgery, unless it leads to a setback. Last thing Knicks need is an injured Houston to go with an injured McDyess.
Knicks lovers can blame Van Horn for everything if they want, but they shouldn't. Not yet, anyway: KVH is averaging 19 ppg and 7.7 rpg.
If Knicks don't start winning when McDyess comes back, the Doc-to-Knicks talk will become a nightly staple.

We're guessing Knicks fans weren't listening when we lobbied for some amnesty for Van Horn. Screamed one at MSG on Wednesday night when it was announced KVH was injured and wouldn't play: "He never does anyway."

Could this little 4-1 run be a sign/warning to delay Dice's comeback a little longer? After three knee surgeries in two years, that certainly wouldn't hurt, even if Dice looks as good in practice as everyone says.
Getting healthier didn't get the Knicks out of going West. Trip is off to 0-3 start ... with Lakers next.
Welcome back, Dice: Knicks roll to an 0-5 trip for just the third time in 25 years. Back home, though, Knicks are 2-1 with Dice.
The city's 24/7 hunt for Knicks scapegoats guarantees that, eventually, even Chaney's string of extensions won't save him from a dismissal. That time appears to be drawing nearer.
A modest two-game win streak is nice, but let's have a little perspective. Routing the Dwyane-less Heat doesn't mean the future is suddenly rosy.
Gone but not forgotten: Knicks' two best players lately are Layden selections: Van Horn (22.9 ppg over past eight games) and Frank Williams.
5-5 record since Isiah's arrival ain't bad. The bad part is how the Knicks can't climb higher than No. 20 in this poll with so many of the league's 20 richest contracts on their payroll now.

Fact that Isiah reportedly offered job to Willis Reed before Wilkens suggests that, yes, Zeke will someday be a coach/GM. In the interim, have to say that Interim Coach Wilkens has exceeded (my) expectations so far.
It's a safe guess that, since committee (of one) took over before last season, Knicks have never been this high. Agreed?
Just when it looks like things are coming together ... Houston's out, Van Horn is ailing and Marbury apparently ain't 100 percent, either.

At 14-9 in the Isiah Era, and with Marbury averaging 10 assists per game as a Knick, it's no stretch to suggest they're suddenly a contender for homecourt advantage in the first round of the playoffs.
It's not all Gotham-based hype. Knicks really do have a great outlook, by East standards, for a team four games under .500.
OK, maybe the Gotham Hype Machine did go a bit overboard. Now Lenny gets to feel the flip side: Adversity, New York-style.
No need to panic, Gotham. Houston is back in the lineup, and we're sure Lenny will think of something else soon.
If Knicks want the No. 6 seed, this is the time to make their move, with seven of 11 at home for the rest of the month and winnable roadies vs. Sixers and Bulls. Plus Houston is back from injury.
It's a good thing Knicks pulled out that comeback in Milwaukee, because everyone else chasing those final three playoff spots in the East had a better week than N.Y. did.
We're not the only ones rooting for Knicks vs. Nets in Round 1. Knicks probably are, too, unless they'd rather face Detroit or Indy.
Houston and Tim Thomas injuries have definitely hurt, but If Celts are in -- as Pierce is promising -- it looks like this is the team on the slide that LeBron must knock out to get to the playoffs.
Perhaps that Knicks-Nets series we've been lobbying for won't be as tasty as we thought. Didn't expect Nets to pound them by 25 with Kidd and K-Mart out.
If nothing else, Knicks have avoided the shame of missing the playoffs for three straight seasons, which hasn't happened in Gotham since 1985-87. But we're guessing the Nets aren't too impressed.

mia.summary: Needed three games to crack the 80-point barrier. With Mavs, Spurs and Wolves next, Heat figures to need a few more games before breaking into the win column.
Sorry. The longer Heat goes without a win ... the worse Riley's timing looks.

Those first two victories helped some, but there's a reason this Van Gundy didn't celebrate too loudly. Sunday started road stretch of Lakers, Seattle, Portland, Golden State, Phoenix ... in span of seven days.
Two weeks ago, Heat was winless. Now Miami has three times as many wins as its Florida rivals.
Maybe the East's Van Gundys aren't as bad as their record looks. Miami is a .500 team when it gets to play in the East.
Hope it wasn't us: After print and TV praise of Haslem, rookie rebounding specialist was moved into bench role.
Standings say Heat is almost a .500 team vs. East opposition (5-6). Stats say Odom (16.5 ppg, 8.8 rpg) doing all he can.
We're seeking forgiveness because we're as guilty as anyone for overlooking Dwyane Wade's fine start. Apology accepted?
Should be a little higher based on its recent 7-3 spike, but Heat just lost Dywane Wade. A really big loss for them.
Stan Van Gundy is 8-3 when he gets to start Odom, Wade, Grant, Eddie and Caron. Of course, that's only happened 33 percent of the time ... and Butler, worringly, looks well shy of 100 percent.
Stan Van Gundy is a .500 coach since that 0-7 start. Alas, now there's little chance he'll keep winning every other game with Wade out.
Maybe things will pick up now that six-game trip out West (1-5) is history. Or maybe not.
Back to .500 if you throw out the 0-7 start. More importantly, Wade is back to help All-Star hopeful Odom.

In spite of all the injuries, Miami has won five of six. Real story, though, is this scary stat: Four coaches in last three years -- Rick Pitino, John Calipari, Frank Johnson and Byron Scott -- lost their jobs right after losing a game in Miami.
After four straight losses -- albeit to good teams -- it's time to forget Lamar Odom's All-Star snub and focus on the playoff chase, because East's No. 8 spot is still up for grabs.
Only a game out of East's eighth spot, which counts for something. Even better: 17 of Miami's final 28 are home games, which obviously helps Heat's chances.
Van Gundy East is a little streaky for our liking, but it looks like Bucher was right: Heat's making a playoff push, with the big shove coming from Wade.
They're the favorites to land the Vin Man, but if Wade is out again that probably won't matter. Heat is 6-10 since Dec. 9 when Wade doesn't play.
All credit to Odom, who has never been better. Back-to-back wins over Bucks and Kings, meanwhile, could be the springboard for a run that gets Heat into the playoffs.
We might be guilty of trotting this one out a time or two before, but it's a stat that still surprises and impresses us: Stan VG is 30-30 as a rookie coach since his 0-7 start.
Miami is 25-24 when Wade is healthy enough to play, and now Heat is three games over .500 if you let us recycle the tired line about throwing out the 0-7 start.

With all the good stories on this team -- Dwyane, Lamar, Stan -- too many of us have overlooked Rafer Alston. He'd actually prefer you don't call him Skip To My Lou these days, and he's giving us plenty of reasons not to.

You know about the 0-7 start. You know we write about it every week. But did you know Heat can be just the third team ever to start 0-7 and finish with a winning record? The others are '82-83 Knicks and '95-96 Cavs.

If you called Stan Van's team clinching a playoff berth before brother Jeff's team, even if you called it before Heat's 0-7 start ... you're flat-out fibbing. Of course, a 5-15 launch isn't so damaging if you finish 15-3.

atl.summary: After three losses by six points or less, and Jason Terry's suspension Monday night, Hawks go West for five. Rough.
On second thought, starting season with seven out of nine on the road might not be so rough. Home games are the lonely ones.
At least they've scratched out a couple nice road wins, at Seattle and at Phoenix. East needs every win it can get these days.
If you're asking us to explain these guys, ask someone else. Hawks are 3-4 against teams with .500-or-better records and 2-5 against teams with losing records.
'Reef is averaging close to 20 and 10 and shooting 51 percent from the field. And getting no closer to that long-awaited first playoff berth.
If Cavs have to suspend Newble again, Hawks would probably take him back, needing every defender they can find.
Stuck in the past? Committee might be guilty because -- big surprise -- we love the green unis. Much as we like so many other retro looks.
They're the anti-Pacers. Indiana hasn't lost two games in a row and Atlanta hasn't won two in a row ... nosediving Hawks are 0-7 after a win.
With Hawks off to worst start since moving to Atlanta in 1968, only solace we can offer is that we're on the short list of fans loving those green throwbacks. For what it's worth.

Still looking for season's first win streak, meaning Hawks still haven't won more than one in a row. Of course, they still don't have new owners officially, so there's a lot of waiting going on in the ATL.
Thought about leaving this space blank to match the effort Hawks gave on this road trip. Just didn't want to confuse the hardy souls who scroll down this far.
Credit where credit is due: We dogged Hawks for dogging it the week before, and then they rebounded to humble Spurs  and us (OK, not us ... but definitely the Spurs).
Surprised Pistons on Sunday, and surprised Spurs before that, but still waiting for first win streak (0-13 after a win) and a 100-point game (O for last 20).
The reward for having the longest tenure of any East coach? Stotts gets to hear Doc Rivers speculation every day.
Now that the Hawks finally know how it feels to win two in a row, perhaps they can work on explaining their 12-18 record vs. winning teams and 5-17 record vs. losing teams.
The advantage to having no fans: You can post an 8-7 uptick, trade away the whole team and no one says a peep. Jokes aside, Hawks' future looks worlds better after the two big trades.
Advice to the new owners, who ignored our advice about keeping 'Sheed at least until the summertime: Please, please, please bring back the Omni organist. That's all we ask.
With two more losses, Hawks will clinch fifth straight losing season. Next Neato Stat for Ernie: Club record is seven straight seasons, from 1950-57.
In the last 30-odd days, Hawks have home wins over Minny, Dallas and Lakers. Of course, after beating L.A. on Tuesday, Hawks lost at Cleveland by 32, then lost at Orlando.
Now you know why Spurs tried to reacquire Stephen Jax at the deadline. He's all Hawks have left, but he just hung 42 on Washington and has been scoring like mad lately.
Don't ask anyone in Atlanta to explain, because no one could even if Philips was full: Hawks are 7-8 against the West's top eight teams, 15-40 against everyone else.
It ain't much consolation, but it's something: Hawks' single-season NBA record for defense (83.4 ppg allowed) looks safe, even with Pistons (84.6) and Spurs (84.9) challenging.
At the risk of offending our loyal Atlanta readers, Hawks are this week's Magic. As in: We're out of pithy comments about these guys.
Still don't know how Hawks lost that Memphis game, but perhaps we shouldn't be surprised. Of its many downfalls this season, Atlanta is 0-6 in OT.

lac.summary: After his first game as an $82 Million Man -- in which he totaled 21 points, 15 boards and EIGHT blocks -- Elton Brand found out he had a hairline fracture in his right foot. Without him, Mike Dunleavy's first month as coach will be seriously rough..
After picking up first win, next assignment is picking up the defense. Clips haven't held anyone under 100 yet, which is a stunner in today's climate.
This probably should have been Stat O' The Week, but it works as a comment, too: Brand-less Clips unbeaten in U.S., winless in Japan.
An 0-3 week means Clips are no longer undefeated in United States, but at least there's some consolation: Brand thinks he'll be back before Christmas.
Loved the throwback unis, with a capital L. The big question now: How long before Q heats up again? His shot's been off since that twisted ankle.
Went a very respectable 6-7 without Brand. Problem is, opponents play them harder when Brand is playing.
Only losses in month of December: Jazz and Kings on the road, Wolves at home by a basket. Clips are overachiveving.

Dunleavy might barely crack most folks' top 5 among Coach of the Year candidates in his own conference. But he's not far off the pace set by Bzdelik, Sloan, Hubie and J. Van Gundy, winning consistently with a stripped-down Clipper ship.
Throw Mike Dunleavy into early Coach of the Year running with no hesitation. Injury-ridden and talent-stripped, Clips are 6-3 since 6-11 start.
The way Clips stoutly defended their goal in the final seconds Sunday night ... they must have thought it was Winner Gets Kobe.
Let's face it: They're not deep enough to withstand a Maggette suspension or another Q injury scare. Not looking forward to that mess of forthcoming road games, either.
Those familiar late-game struggles have resurfaced, and there's worse news: Lots of road games (18 out of 25) beckon after Friday.
Can't complain too much about a 36-win pace after losing more key free agents than they kept (four to two) and losing Brand early to injury.
For all that Brand, Maggette and Q do, Clips just endured a 1-7 road slump that only ended Saturday because Magic didn't have T-Mac.
Moved to within three games of .500 with a 3-1 start on their eight-game trip, only to lose at Washington and New York. Worse yet, a back-to-back in Minnesota and Memphis looms.

You can deal with a four-game losing streak and the All-Star snubs of Brand and Maggette a bit better when you know you've made the top two on Kobe's list of free-agent destinations. List consists of Lakes and Clips.
They'll need a 17-11 finish to avoid the 11th straight losing season in franchise history. What's your bet?
Clips quietly sported a five-game home winning streak before Detroit snapped it Sunday ... but a streak that modest ain't going to grab much attention out West.
A 4-11 slide edges Clips ever closer to their 11th straight losing season. The record is 15 if you're curious: Sacramento from 1983-98.
We really wish Kobe would hurry up and defect to Clips because it's getting tougher to come up something here that meets our usual standards.
Dunleavy's right. Clips will eventually need a (real) practice facility, if for no other reason except that Kobe would want a state-of-the-art place to park his Ducati.
On a dreadful 2-16 run, Clips have secured their 11th consecutive losing season. To go with the 12-season drought from 1979-91.

In a once-glorious history, albeit glorious only if you include the Buffalo part, Clips have only 11 seasons out of 34 with less than 50 losses ... and one of them was the lockout season. When they only played 50.

Just in case Clips feel better after reading the Golden State comment ... don't forget that L.A.'s JV holds the NBA record with 15 straight seasons out of the playoffs ... and just extended its current drought to seven.
